scope: Read-only repo implementation/content review; no app or database mutations. Existing artifacts are evidence, not fresh production readback. RW defect sample retrieved from preserved initial backup;48of54exam1RW IDs recovered there. This is INITIAL, not a post-repair certification.

official_prompt_conflicts.finding: Official College Board Math overview says questions across each module arranged easiest to hardest. User Part3 forbids simple ascending M1 progression; official-source override supports ascending Math while retaining meaningful easy/medium/hard mixture.

scoring_policy.weights: equal for applicable variables unless future approved rubric supplies weights
scoring_policy.null_policy: Unmeasurable dimensions remain null; null is not zero or passing. Overall certified weighted score withheld if any applicable dimension unmeasured. Editorial estimates are not empirical calibration or official test-equivalence evidence.
scoring_policy.scoring_equivalence: No valid official equated SAT/ACT scoring model is established. Raw accuracy and linear analytics estimates must remain labeled as practice estimates.
scoring_policy.copyright_check: Authorship provenance and no official source copying are documented, but exhaustive similarity to all protected items cannot be proved without licensed corpus; do not assert universal originality verification.

variables.name: Structure accuracy
variables.evidence: Four equal SAT modules exist; no scheduled ten-minute inter-section break; only Math adapts.

variables.name: Timing accuracy
variables.evidence: 32/32/35/35 minute module limits correct. Ten-minute break absent; timeout requires manual submission rather than enforced boundary.

variables.name: Section/question-count accuracy
variables.evidence: 36 saved blueprints and validation report contain 98 administered items, 54 RW and44 Math,27/27/22/22.

variables.name: Domain distribution
variables.evidence: Math all paths15/15/7/7 satisfies official13–15/13–15/5–7/5–7 ranges. RW target14 Information/14 Craft/12 Expression/14 Conventions approximates distribution but Craft slightly underweighted; classification quality unverified.

variables.name: Skill distribution
variables.evidence: Math covers19 official skills; frequency not independently calibrated against representative official design. RW taxonomy labels cannot remedy invalid/mismatched stimuli.

variables.name: Difficulty distribution
variables.evidence: Math M1 6easy/12medium/4hard; easier M2 10/10/2; harder M2 2/10/10. RW lacks separate routes; labels editorial.

variables.name: Difficulty authenticity
variables.evidence: Empirical item difficulty/ability-stratified correctness/response-time evidence absent. No legitimate measured authenticity percentage.

variables.name: Question archetype authenticity
variables.evidence: Math includes parameter reasoning and SPR. RW standalone grammar sentences and generic study-note prompts depart from authentic academic stimulus architecture.

variables.name: Passage authenticity
variables.evidence: Recovered RW sample recycles ferry/library/clay/plant scenarios and repeated study notes; longer shared passages coexist with very short fragments.

variables.name: Vocabulary authenticity
variables.evidence: Recovered sample tests lasted with implausible alternatives photographed/billed/banned; no demonstrated upper-range contextual vocabulary bank.

variables.name: Math reasoning authenticity
variables.evidence: 132 original Math items include identities, parameter systems, rational/radical constraints, nonlinear reasoning. Some declared hard tasks are standard discriminant/parallel-line computations. Empirical top-end discrimination unknown.

variables.name: Answer-choice authenticity
variables.evidence: Math98MC/34SPR bank; every full path33MC/11SPR. Math answer letters30A/27B/17C/24D (98MC), not uniform but no demonstrated sequence pattern. RW all-wrong/truncated-key examples invalidate quality.

variables.name: Distractor quality
variables.evidence: Numerical choices frequently reflect student errors, but no explicit per-choice rationale field. RW sample contains irrelevant/comically implausible choices and no defensible correct choice in identified case.

variables.name: Graph/data representation
variables.evidence: Only5 explicitly authored SVG figures across132 Math items; some full paths have zero supplied figures. Quantitative RW stimulus quality not established.

variables.name: Contextual problem distribution
variables.evidence: No contextual-problem metadata or independent contextual-count classifier; approximately30% official Math target cannot be verified.

variables.name: Adaptive behavior — SAT
variables.evidence: Math raw threshold15/22 routes easier/harder under authenticated RPC; no RW routing. Threshold is practice approximation, not calibrated official behavior.

variables.name: ACT pacing — ACT
variables.evidence: Not applicable to SAT.

variables.name: Calculator/tool realism
variables.evidence: Desmos available, but tool UI also exposes AI chat/hints during full test; calculator expectations are not separated robustly by SAT RW vsMath and ACT.

variables.name: Content diversity
variables.evidence: Math bank132 shared across36 exams with recurrence. RW examples repeatedly recycle a small subject/scenario set; no topic/name/archetype history gate.

variables.name: Overall test-taking experience
variables.evidence: Authenticated flow/resume/server scoring validated. Missing break, available tutor assistance, no RW adaptivity and uncalibrated score estimates prevent high-fidelity full-test claim.

repair_priorities.repair: Distinct section sizes, times, passage groups, optional Science, nonadaptive flow, and bank taxonomy; preserve legacy performance IDs.

repair_priorities.issue: Rebuild RW bank rather than reuse weak templates
repair_priorities.repair: Original diverse short academic stimuli, four plausible choices, independent best-answer review, proper quantitative evidence, and two Module 2 routes.
Separate learning from strict simulation; disable tutor/hints in strict mode, restrict calculator by exam/section, add durable ten-minute SAT break and server-backed module deadlines.
Require per-choice rationales, estimated solve time, subskill/module eligibility, graphic-data consistency, independent blind solutions, and release-gate records before persistence.
Track original graphic requirements per blueprint with independent data verification; measure contextual Math frequency rather than infer from labels.
Capture item time, skips, answer changes, distractor choices, and ability-stratified outcomes; label editorial difficulty provisional until sample is adequate. Do not invent scores of 95 or higher.
Larger diverse validated bank, exposure-aware blueprint selection, and near-duplicate semantic review.
